correctness.rationale: Because the basis squares form a basis, two distinct image columns of a natural basis cannot both have a nonzero entry in any given row. Invertibility forces a monomial change of basis, whose support permutation is a directed graph isomorphism. On an ordered cycle of length ℓ, iterating the scaling recurrence shows that the necessary and sufficient closure condition is P′/P=u_0^{2^ℓ−1}; one initial solution gives a unique full scaling. Advancing the origin changes P to P²/a_{i_0}^{2^ℓ−1}, so the quotient class transforms by squaring and rotations give exactly its squaring orbit. In the cyclic quotient of order g_ℓ the r-fold fixed set has gcd(g_ℓ,2^r−1) members, proving the Burnside count. Unordered multisets give the Euler product. A cycle at orbit length d_t admits ℓ/d_t rotations with g_ℓ lifts each; components can be permuted only within type and give the factorials. Iterating x_{σ(i)}=a_i x_i² gives all-zero coordinates on a cycle or the closure equation x_{i_0}^{2^ℓ−1}=P⁻¹, with exactly g_ℓ nonzero-coordinate solutions for the identity label. Counts multiply on independent components. A nonidentity label first occurs when ℓ is divisible by ord_p(2) for an odd prime p dividing q−1, and every component in an idempotent-free algebra must have a nonidentity label. The one-component construction therefore attains the minimum. The q−1=1 case is included as 2⁰. For F₄ in dimension two the two-cycle quotient has one fixed identity and one orbit of length two, giving automorphism orders 6 and 3 and idempotent counts 4 and 1; the two-loop algebra is a third type. The supplied checker was inspected, not run; this proof uses no finite-range extrapolation.
